extracted.intended_audience: comedians, festival participants, industry professionals, and general readers interested in the Edinburgh Festival Fringe awards
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, eligibility conditions, and selection criteria for the Edinburgh Comedy Awards (formerly Perrier Awards) presented to comedy shows at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main prize criterion (The Donald and Eleanor Taffner Best Comedy Show)
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded "for the funniest, most outstanding, up-and-coming comic / comedy show / act" at the Fringe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The winner receives a cash prize of £10,000. Historically the main prize was for many years the only prize. There have been joint winners (e.g., 2017) and exceptions in past years (e.g., 2008 the prize was awarded to "every comedian on the Fringe").

rubrics_metrics.name: DLT Entertainment Best Newcomer Award eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Given to the best "performer or act who is performing their first full-length show (50 minutes or more)".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduced in 1992. The Best Newcomer winner receives a cash prize of £5,000. Newcomers are eligible for the Best Comedy Show Award as well, but see the shortlist exclusivity rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortlist exclusivity between Newcomer and Best Comedy Show
rubrics_metrics.description: No act is allowed to appear on both shortlists in the same year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although newcomers are eligible for the Best Comedy Show Award, procedural rules prevent a single act appearing on both the Newcomer and Best Comedy Show shortlists in the same year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel Prize eligibility and discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: All shows are eligible for the Panel Prize, and the award may not be awarded at all, if the panel so choose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Panel Prize was inaugurated in 2006. Like Best Newcomer, the Panel Prize winner receives a cash prize (historically £5,000). The panel has wide discretion: in some years it has chosen joint winners or no winner (no panel prize awarded in 2017; in 2008 it was awarded to all performers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards are presented to shows deemed 'the best' at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe
rubrics_metrics.description: The Edinburgh Comedy Awards are presented to the comedy shows deemed to have been the best at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe in Scotland.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This frames the awards as festival-focused recognitions rather than general career awards; winners have often gone on to greater success. Selection is made by the awards' judging panel (organisers/directors have included Nica Burns since 1984).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and judging by panel (judging body discretion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Winners are chosen by a judging panel which can exercise discretion including awarding joint winners or withholding an award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: joint winners for Best Show in 2017; Panel Prize withheld in some years; Panel Prize awarded to all performers in 2008. The exact composition of the judging panel and its revealed shortlists are part of the awards' procedures (references to judging panel announcements are present).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prize amounts and sponsorship/naming
rubrics_metrics.description: Cash prizes and the awards' names have varied with sponsorship (e.g., Perrier, Intelligent Finance, Foster's, lastminute.com, Dave, Sky TV, DLT Entertainment, The Victoria Wood Foundation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical contemporary cash awards cited: £10,000 for the main prize, £5,000 for other prizes. Sponsorship changes have led to frequent renaming of the awards (hence the colloquial 'the Eddie' to avoid sponsor confusion). Sponsorship history does not change stated eligibility criteria but affects naming and public perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical and inclusivity criticisms as evaluative concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: The awards have faced criticism for lack of diversity (e.g., shortlists with no female acts or nominees all male/white/English and concentrated at a single venue).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not a formal criterion listed by the awards, these criticisms function as public evaluative standards and have informed discussion about how the awards reflect representation at the Fringe (examples: criticisms in 2002 and 2009; Rose Matafeo in 2018 noted as first non-white solo winner).
